findings.conditions: variable-order (hp) ParFiniteElementSpace on a parallel NC mesh; a NeighborOrderMessage Isend'ed before MPI_Barrier has not yet arrived when the IProbe(MPI_ANY_SOURCE) loop runs
findings.reasoning: OrderPropagation sends order messages with IsendAll, calls MPI_Barrier and then drains with a non-blocking IProbe(ANY_SOURCE, NEIGHBOR_ORDER_VM) loop. A barrier does not guarantee that previously posted point-to-point messages are visible to MPI_Iprobe, so the loop can exit before a neighbour's message arrives. That message is either thrown away by the following drain loop, or left queued and picked up by the IProbe of a later OrderPropagation call (next iteration or next Update), where it is decoded against different edge/face numbering. Missing or stale order bits leave edge/face orders inconsistent between ranks; 'changed' may stay false everywhere so the do-while in fespace.cpp terminates with mismatched variable-order DOFs, giving a wrong prolongation or later failures. Whether it happens depends on message timing.

findings.conditions: parallel NC (or hp) space; a rank reaches num_finalized == ndofs while neighbours still have NeighborRowMessages (forwarded or redundant rows) in flight; space rebuilt later (Update / another space on the same mesh)
findings.reasoning: BuildParallelConformingInterpolation polls with IProbe(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, NEIGHBOR_ROW_VM) and leaves its main loop as soon as its own DOFs are finalized. Neighbours may still send rows (forwarding, rows of shared DOFs already finalized). The cleanup at 4570 only drops messages that have already arrived; later ones stay queued under the same tag and communicator and are matched by this IProbe in the next call to BuildParallelConformingInterpolation. Decode then interprets the stale rows with the new mesh/space numbering, so they can overwrite pmatrix rows, increment num_finalized wrongly, index out of range (crash), or give a wrong P/R matrix. Which message gets matched depends on arrival timing.

findings.conditions: hp space; an order message from a neighbour arrives between the end of the receive loop (3714) and the cleanup IProbe loop
findings.reasoning: Right after the receiving IProbe loop exits on 'no message yet', a second IProbe(MPI_ANY_SOURCE) loop RecvDrops whatever has arrived in the meantime. A genuine message of the current round that arrives in that window is matched by the cleanup probe and discarded without its orders being OR'ed into edge_orders/face_orders, and 'changed' is not set. The neighbour does not resend it, because it only resends orders that changed on its side, so the receiving rank can keep a lower order on a shared edge/face than its neighbour. That gives inconsistent DOF sets across ranks, so the parallel interpolation is wrong or BuildParallelConformingInterpolation never finalizes and hangs.

findings.conditions: RecvAll used by RecvRebalanceDofs (mesh/pncmesh.cpp:2905) or the ghost-rank exchange (2641) when one rank has moved on to the next exchange with the same tag (e.g. RebalanceMatrix of a second space) while another is still receiving
findings.reasoning: RecvAll counts messages, not senders: Probe(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, Tag) matches any message with the tag, and the code itself notes there is no guard against two messages from the same rank. If a fast rank already sent its message for the next exchange with the same tag (no collective in between), the slow rank can take it in place of a missing sender's message. It overwrites rank_msg[rank], reaches recv_left == 0, and the missing message is then consumed by the next exchange, so element DOFs are mapped to the wrong elements or offsets (wrong rebalance matrix; the debug assert catches only an unexpected rank).

findings.conditions: 2D conforming parallel LocalRefinement; another tag-0-class message from the same neighbour on MyComm is pending (Isend requests here are never waited, and tag 0 is also NEIGHBOR_ELEMENT_RANK_VM)
findings.reasoning: The receive of edge splittings uses MPI_ANY_TAG with a fixed count edges_in_group, while the sends use tag 0 and their MPI_Request is overwritten without ever being completed. Any other pending message from the same neighbour on MyComm, whatever its tag, can be matched instead. A larger message aborts with MPI_ERR_TRUNCATE, and a different one makes iBuf garbage, so refinement differs across ranks (non-conforming mesh, inconsistent need_refinement). Which message matches depends on what is still in flight.
